paper: A New DTMOS MOS-C Implementation of Fractional-Order Low-Voltage Low-Power Differentiator/High-Pass Filter
evidence: Figure5(a): FF,FS,SF,SS; Figure5(b): ±0.7,±0.8,±1.0,±1.1 V; Figure5(c): −27,0,+27,+100 °C. Nominal±0.9V from TableII. Paper varies axes separately, not full Cartesian product. NN27C used for unspecified fixed axes.
sizing: Latest native-verified17MOS private HPF candidate; no extra feedback devices; exact device sizing frozen
limitations: M2 drain current remains approximately 0.9 pA and IN is approximately −0.89999964 V, close to VSS. The intended active three-branch operating condition has not been recovered.

The measured response is a useful near-first-order high-pass candidate. It is not validated as the paper’s fractional-order implementation or as a reproduction of its complete internal operating mode.

STB probes only the internal N2→M4-gate loop. Its loop gain remains below unity throughout 1 mHz–10 GHz, so phase margin and gain margin are undefined; no numeric fallback is used. This does not establish stability of every possible feedback loop or loading condition.
Output current is measured into an ideal 0 V clamp. Output compliance and loading sensitivity are not validated.
Only NN, 27 °C, ±0.9 V was tested. No process or temperature corners were added.
